extracted.intended_audience: NLP / machine-learning researchers and practitioners working on political-bias detection in news articles
extracted.subtask_description: Predict the leading political ideology (left, center, right) of individual news articles using supervised learning; includes dataset creation, debiasing methods, and evaluation under splits that control for source leakage. Focuses on article-level labels rather than media-level distant supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article-level manual annotation (left/center/right)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and annotate news articles at the article level with political ideology labels: left, center, or right. The dataset created contains 34,737 articles annotated at the article level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use article-level labels rather than projecting media-level labels to every article (distant supervision). Ensure the dataset spans a wide variety of topics and media and that left/center/right perspectives are balanced across topics and media. Note: 'center' denotes centrist political ideology, not absence of political content (i.e., center is a substantive class distinct from non-political articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation quality / AllSides rigorous process
rubrics_metrics.description: Source article labels from a platform (AllSides) that uses a rigorous multi-step annotation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AllSides' process includes blind bias surveys, editorial reviews, third-party analysis, independent reviews, and community feedback. Prefer such multi-method annotation procedures for higher-quality article-level labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced coverage across topics and media
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset should represent topics or events from different political perspectives so classifiers learn ideology signals rather than topic correlations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect articles for many topics (paper: 109 topics) and many media (paper: 73 media), and ensure for frequent topics that left/center/right labels are represented (paper claims dataset is well-balanced across topics and media). When sampling triplets or splits, consider topic overlap to control topic-induced similarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding source leakage via dataset splits
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a media-based split where test articles come from media that were not seen during training, to prevent models from learning to identify the article's source instead of its political ideology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create (i) Media-based Split: sample test articles from a subset of media and exclude remaining articles from those media from training, ensuring all articles from the same medium appear in only one of train/dev/test sets; and (ii) Random Split for comparison (typical practice). Use the media-based split for robust evaluation of ideology prediction generalization to unseen sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-processing to remove explicit source markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove explicit markers that reveal the source (e.g., author name, medium name in article preamble or content) to reduce trivial signals for source identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strip author and medium mentions and other explicit identifiers before training so the model must rely on linguistic/semantic signals rather than explicit metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics: Accuracy, macro-F1, and MAE (ordinal-aware)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate models using accuracy and macro-F1 (F1 averaged across classes), and report Mean Absolute Error (MAE) to account for the ordinal nature of labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use macro-F1 as an early stopping criterion due to class imbalance; compute MAE as 1/N sum |yi - ŷi| to reflect ordinal distance between predicted and true labels. Report all three metrics to capture different aspects of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting / measuring source-modeling tendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether a model is learning to predict the medium from the article content (i.e., source leakage) by formulating a media-prediction experiment (multi-way classification over media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train a classifier to predict the medium (paper: 73-way classification) and compare model performance to majority baseline; strong performance indicates models can easily learn source-specific signals and that special care (de-biasing) is required for ideology prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adversarial Media Adaptation (AA) for de-biasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an adversarial adaptation architecture (encoder + label predictor + media classifier with gradient reversal) so the encoder learns representations discriminative for ideology while invariant across media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jointly minimize label predictor loss and maximize media classifier loss (implemented via gradient reversal). Control the trade-off with hyperparameter λ (paper varied 0–1; best λ=0.7). This reduces encoder reliance on media-specific stylistic cues and improves generalization to unseen media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triplet Loss Pre-training (TLP) for de-biasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-train the encoder using a triplet loss so examples with the same ideology (but different media) are closer while examples of different ideology (possibly from same medium) are farther apart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct triplets (anchor, positive, negative) where positive shares ideology but is from a different medium, and negative has different ideology but may be from same medium. Sample triplets that discuss the same topic to minimize topic-induced distance (paper sampled ~35,017 triplets). After pre-training, fine-tune encoder + softmax on main task. TLP showed large improvements on media-based split.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporating media-level representations as complementary features
rubrics_metrics.description: Complement article encoding with media-level representations (e.g., Twitter followers' bios, Wikipedia page content) concatenated before the softmax classifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encode Twitter followers' bios with Sentence-BERT and average up to 1,000 followers per medium; encode Wikipedia page content with BERT (average second-to-last-layer word representations). Concatenate these media features with article encoding; combined with de-biased article representations, this yields sizable gains (Twitter bios more helpful than Wikipedia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Model architectures and hyperparameter tuning for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Use both LSTM-based and Transformer-based (BERT) architectures; tune input length, layers, cell size, dropout, learning rate, gradient clipping and batch size on validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper's best LSTM settings: 512-token input, 2-layer LSTM size 256, dropout 0.7, learning rate 1e-3, gradient clipping 0.5, batch size 32 (≈1.1M params, GloVe 300-d inputs). BERT: 512-token input, learning rate 2e-5, gradient clipping 1 (≈110M params). Fix random seeds for reproducibility; report hardware/training time (paper: 4 Titan X Pascal GPUs; epoch runtimes: ~25s LSTM, ~22min BERT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Triplet sampling constraints (topic control)
rubrics_metrics.description: When sampling triplets for TLP, select examples that discuss the same topic to ensure topic similarity does not dominate embedding distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constrain triplets so anchor/positive/negative share topic to reduce topic-induced proximity; this helps the encoder cluster by ideology rather than by topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of dataset, splits, and code for extension and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the dataset, evaluation splits (media-based and random), and code to allow others to reproduce and extend the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish train/validation/test splits and code repository so researchers can extend the dataset as more articles are added and compare fairly (paper released data and splits on GitHub).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability / explainability desideratum
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that predict media or article ideology should enable explainability—e.g., pinpoint specific articles or fragments that support a media-level classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not fully developed in this work, the authors highlight explainability as important for downstream applications (e.g., identifying fragments where bias occurs) and for allowing media-level labels to be supported by article-level evidence.
